concerns.advisory: The write lock is acquired with `defer` before the entire asset-loading body, so the exclusive lock is held across manifest file reads, JSON parsing, and licensing calls — in `setting.Dev` mode the cache is never consulted, so every single request serializes behind that lock and does full file I/O.
concerns.why: `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock(); defer entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Unlock()` is placed immediately before `var err error; var result *dtos.EntryPointAssets` and the subsequent load path, and the fast-path early return is gated on `cfg.Env != setting.Dev`.

concerns.advisory: The lock upgrade is not a proper double-checked lock: after taking the write lock the code never re-reads `entryPointAssetsCache`, so N concurrent cold-start requests each redo the full asset load and each overwrite the cache, wasting work on startup even though the result is correct.
concerns.why: The read-lock snapshot `ret := entryPointAssetsCache` is taken and released, then `Lock()` is taken with no second `if entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return ... }` check inside the critical section.

concerns.advisory: No test accompanies this concurrency fix, so the race it repairs (and any future regression, e.g. someone reintroducing an unguarded read) would not be caught — this needs a `-race` test that calls `GetWebAssets` from multiple goroutines.
concerns.why: The diff touches only `webassets.go`; no `webassets_test.go` change is included alongside the new `sync.RWMutex`.

concerns.why: `return ret, nil` returns the shared cached pointer rather than a copy, and `dtos.EntryPointAssets` fields are exported and mutable.
